rationale:
THE BASE HALF of the cpp cross-file `overrides` pin, and it is pinned for its own sake rather than as an accessory — the pattern php/cross-file-override-base established. `cross-file-override.cpp`'s forbid rows are only meaningful against a KNOWN declaration set: `inheritedOnly`, `neverRedeclared` and `NonVirtualBase` are here precisely so that 'the base does not declare it' and 'the base declares it non-virtually' are checkable rather than assumed.

Four distinct things have to be told apart, and this is the fixture for telling them apart:
  - `step` is pure virtual, so a subclass declaring `void step(int) override` genuinely overrides it. Provable cross-file from the KEYWORD plus THIS declaration.
  - `tune` is virtual WITH A BODY and is redeclared with a different parameter type. That is C++ NAME HIDING, not an override — the exact confusion the M37.9 differential round recorded when it excluded cpp overrides from the oracle ('same-name across a base chain conflates C++ NAME-HIDING with virtual override ... different arity hides, it does not override').
  - `probe` is virtual with a body and is redeclared WITHOUT the keyword. On a name-only cross-file companion it is INDISTINGUISHABLE from `tune`, which is why the resolver refuses a companion-only match (see the subclass fixture).
  - `step` also exists on `ExternalSidecar` and on `NonVirtualBase`. Two of those three are the leaf-name collision a cross-file lookup has to survive, and the third is the non-virtual case where no `overrides` edge may be published at all however it is spelled.

expectSymbols.name: inheritedOnly
expectSymbols.note: NOT redeclared by the subclass. Inheriting is not overriding.

expectSymbols.name: step
expectSymbols.note: the same leaf name as ExternalInterface::step, in a different class — the collision a cross-file lookup must survive.

expectSymbols.name: step
expectSymbols.note: NON-VIRTUAL: a same-name method here is plain hiding and no `overrides` edge may name it.

forbidRelationships.note: `ExternalSidecar` declares no base-class clause at all, so there is no `implements` edge for it in either direction — asserted here rather than left to the reader, because the whole point of `ExternalSidecar::step` is to share a LEAF NAME with `ExternalInterface::step`, and a resolver that matched on the leaf could invent this edge.
and no `extends` edge either — the leaf-name collision must not become an inheritance claim.
